text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- More social security income being spent on increasingly costly social security schemes. (p1)
- Unilever wants soyabean processing industry to continue search for ways to to separate genetic and natural beans. (p1)
- Retailer Ahold plans to use latest takeover in Brazil as bridgehead for further South American expansion. (p1)
- Philips sacks Geoffrey Carroll, chief of its Origin automation unit. (p3)
- Hoogovens maintains earlier H2 profit forecasts. (p3)
- Financial services group ING and insurer Aegon both win life-insurance licences in the Philippines. (p4)
- Brewer Heineken may lose Zaire business locations due to violence in the region. (p4)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Dutch save less in third quarter -- CBS. (p2)
- Walloon rival Cockerill-Sambre vies with Hoogovens in battle for Belgian steel firm Boel. (p2)
- Schiedam-based transporter Ebrex and Seaport Terminals in Rotterdam to build fruit terminal. (p2)
- Robeco's property division Rodamco sees 1997 profit growth. (p15)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Robin Linschoten, forced to quit as junior minister earlier this year, appointed manager at Rabobank's Interpolis insurance unit. (p1)
- Generale Bank follows ABN AMRO in changing 36-hour working week back to 40-hours for certain staff. (p23)
- Employers association (VNO-NCW) wants businesses meeting environmental targets to be rewarded. (p23)
- KLM October load factor up to 76 (74.6) pct. (p25)
TROUW
- KLM mulls engine maintenance joint-venture with U.S. General Electric. (p7)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Sports-only commercial TV station Sport7 loses Dfl 400,000 a day, according to TROS news programme. (p1)
- Fiasco over sale of 40 percent stake in Content temp agency owned by chair Sylvia Toth. (p11)
